whatIs: AI agent development is the design and engineering of software that is given a goal, works out the steps, and uses tools — your CRM, catalogue, inbox, ERP or the web — to complete the task, asking a person for approval where the stakes are high. A chatbot answers and an automation follows fixed rules; an agent decides what to do next based on what it finds.

At gaa-tha every agent starts as a written job description: what it may read, which actions it may take, what it must escalate and how success is measured. We choose the model per task, connect tools through function calling and MCP servers, ground answers in your documents with retrieval (RAG), and ship with an evaluation set, cost limits and a trace of every step, so you can always see why the agent did what it did.

faq.q: What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot or an automation?
faq.a: An AI agent is software that is given a goal and a set of tools and decides the steps itself to reach it. A chatbot answers questions in a conversation, and an automation follows fixed if-this-then-that rules; an agent can look up a CRM record, check stock, draft a reply and ask for approval without each step being scripted. Most production systems combine all three, with the agent handling only the steps that need judgement.

faq.q: What kinds of AI agents can gaa-tha build?
faq.a: We build lead-qualification and sales agents that research inbound enquiries and draft follow-ups, support agents that resolve order and policy questions, research agents that compile market or competitor briefs, operations agents that check order status and inventory and generate reports, and content agents that draft listings and posts in your brand voice. Each starts with one narrow job and expands once it performs on measured tests.

faq.q: Which AI model is best for building an agent — Claude, GPT or Gemini?
faq.a: There is no single best model; the right choice depends on the task, so we test candidates on your own examples before deciding. Claude, GPT and Gemini differ in tool use, long-document handling, language coverage, speed and price, and smaller or open-source models are often good enough for classification and extraction at a fraction of the cost. We build model-agnostic so you can switch when a better or cheaper model ships.

faq.q: How much does an AI agent cost to build and run?
faq.a: Build cost is driven by the number of tools and systems the agent connects to, the data preparation and retrieval it needs, the approval and security requirements, and how many edge cases must be handled. Running cost is mostly model usage per task, which we control with model routing, caching and token budgets and report monthly. A narrow agent on one system costs far less than a multi-agent workflow spanning ERP, CRM and WhatsApp.

faq.q: Is our data safe, and will the AI models train on it?
faq.a: Agents are built on the paid API and business tiers of the major model providers, which by default do not use your inputs to train their models; free consumer apps can have different terms, so we never build on them. Agents run in your own cloud and provider accounts, read only what their permissions allow, and log every action. For highly sensitive data we can use region-specific hosting or an open-source model on your own servers.

faq.q: How do you deal with hallucinations and accuracy?
faq.a: AI agents can make mistakes, so accuracy is engineered and measured rather than assumed. We ground answers in your documents with citations, restrict actions to defined tools, instruct the agent to say when it does not know, and re-run an evaluation set of real cases after every change. High-impact actions such as refunds, price changes or outbound messages stay behind human approval until measured accuracy justifies relaxing it.

faq.q: Who owns the agent, the prompts and the code?
faq.a: You do. Code, prompts, evaluation sets and MCP servers live in a repository in your name, model and cloud accounts are yours, and everything is documented at handover. You can run, change or move the agent without gaa-tha.

faq.q: How do I choose an AI agent development company?
faq.a: Choose a team that starts from a business process rather than a model, shows how it measures accuracy, explains cost per task, and builds in your accounts with no lock-in. Ask how they handle permissions, approvals and logging, which models they tested for your use case, and what happens when a model is updated or retired. Be cautious of anyone promising full autonomy or guaranteed results before seeing your data.
